evals.name: treatment-decision-answer-and-depth
evals.prompt: Research the evidence for using prazosin in PTSD-related nightmares — I've got a patient in clinic this afternoon.
evals.expected_output: Builds a decision brief for a treatment choice (the decision, the verdict's shape = a dose + what not to promise, what settles it, mandatory publication-bias check) rather than sorting the request into a named frame. Because the reader is deciding under time pressure, the chosen shape sensibly puts the verdict first — explicitly marked, naming a dose range and an explicit confidence level with the one-clause reason it isn't higher. The load-bearing trials each get the full per-study treatment: the small positive crossover RCTs and the large negative multisite RCT are laid out with design, population, n, comparator, endpoint, and effect size with CI before the adjudication lands — never compressed to a clause. Adjudicates rather than listing. Every section contains a number. NO inline citations anywhere in prose. ## Sources is one line per source: topic phrase + DOI link only — no authors, journal, year, or PMID. ClinicalTrials.gov was queried. No atomic note produced.

evals.name: topic-shape-legal-answer-required
evals.prompt: Give me an evidence review of ketamine for treatment-resistant depression — I want to actually understand it, not just get a bottom line.
evals.expected_output: Shape is chosen for the question: because the user asked to UNDERSTAND, a topic-shaped structure (e.g. how it is meant to work → what the trials show → what the harms cost → verdict) is legitimate and appropriate — topic-domain headings like Mechanism or Adverse effects are allowed structure, not banned. What is NOT negotiable: an explicit, marked verdict must exist (it may close rather than lead, but a skimmer finds it in seconds, with a confidence level and the one clause it is not higher); mechanism/background is woven in at real depth; every load-bearing trial carries design, population, n, comparator, endpoint, effect size + CI; disagreements are adjudicated, not catalogued. FAILS if the report is an unanswered survey with no marked verdict, or if load-bearing studies are compressed to name-plus-conclusion clauses. Routes through intent-lock first (or on explicit opt-out builds the brief itself and names the reading it took).

evals.name: service-decision-and-registry
evals.prompt: Should we build an rTMS service at Klaeng for treatment-resistant depression? What does the evidence say.
evals.expected_output: Builds the brief for a service decision: the verdict is build / don't / build-under-conditions, with throughput and staff-time implications in the units the hospital uses, explicitly marked wherever the chosen shape places it. Quantifies remission rate, sessions per course, durability at 6 and 12 months, and cost or staff-hours per responder — pragmatic effectiveness over efficacy — with the load-bearing effectiveness trials each given full per-study detail. ClinicalTrials.gov is load-bearing here: surfaces ongoing large trials with expected readout and any terminated trials, placed with the forward-looking evidence (what would change the verdict). Does not answer with efficacy literature alone. NCT numbers appear in Sources with status, n, endpoint, readout. Depth follows what the evidence contains — no real finding is cut for leanness, no padding added to look thorough.

evals.name: thai-trigger-contested-claim
evals.prompt: มีคนบอกว่า SSRIs ทำให้ suicidality เพิ่มในวัยรุ่น จริงหรือเปล่า ช่วยค้น PubMed ให้หน่อย
evals.expected_output: Triggers on Thai. Builds the brief for a contested claim: the verdict is true/false/unsettled PLUS why the disagreement exists, explicitly marked (leading is the natural choice here since the claim is the whole question); if unsettled, names the specific experiment that would settle it. Adjudicates by design and power, never by counting papers. Reports the replication series in chronological order with each pivotal study's design, n, and effect size — effect-size drift shown study by study, not asserted. Prose is clean of inline attributions. The report is as deep as the evidence base deserves: a simply resolvable claim may need few sections, but the load-bearing analyses are never reduced to clauses. Response prose to the user is in Thai-English code-switch; the report file itself may be English.

evals.name: teaching-decision-textbook-gap
evals.prompt: I'm lecturing residents on delirium management next week. What can I safely say about first-line pharmacotherapy?
evals.expected_output: Builds the brief for a teaching decision: the verdict's shape is the verbatim sentence to be spoken aloud, with one memorable correct number, plus its expiry conditions — explicitly marked. Open Library is load-bearing: names a canonical text with a real edition and OLID. The body covers the textbook-vs-evidence gap: explicitly flags where the textbook and current evidence diverge, states which position the trainee should hold and which they should merely recognize on an exam, and gives the trials behind the divergence full per-study detail. Does not silently resolve the divergence in favour of the literature.

evals.name: atomize-gate-closed
evals.prompt: Look up the evidence on lithium for suicide prevention in bipolar disorder.
evals.expected_output: Report only. NO atomic note, NO vault frontmatter, NO MOC wiring, NO meta-bind button — the word 'atomize' was never said. Chat response is two lines: what was delivered, PubMed N / trials N / books N, the verdict's confidence, any [unverified] gaps. The report file is presented; its contents are NOT restated inline beyond the default show step.

evals.name: atomize-gate-open
evals.prompt: Look up the evidence on lithium for suicide prevention in bipolar disorder, then atomize it for my vault.
evals.expected_output: Report AND an atomic note produced. The note uses ordinary concept headings (Mechanism, Dosing, Efficacy) because a note has no decision to spine on. To create it, the skill follows atomic-note-template.md to assemble title (Concept — Qualifier) and body, then HANDS OFF to vault-keeper rather than acting on the vault itself: it passes title, body, target type (note/artifact), suggested MOC topic, source-skill identity/tags, plus optional extra frontmatter fields (sources with PMID/DOI, board_pearls, review_count: 0, last_reviewed, aliases) as a flat map. The skill itself never dedup-greps the vault, never resolves a vault path, and never writes YAML frontmatter or content into vault/ directly — vault-keeper owns paths, dedup, MOC wiring, and the index, and reports back what it did. The report file still lands per the default write → show → file pipeline: written to the working directory (or report_dir from .pubmed-research-note.json), shown inline, AND handed to vault-keeper as an artifact by default — 'atomize' adds the atomic-note handoff on top; it does not gate the report's own vault filing. No fabricated vault path is ever printed by this skill.

evals.name: negative-trigger-daily-digest
evals.prompt: Give me today's psychiatry paper digest across all the subspecialties.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT trigger. There is no decision attached and the request is a multi-domain daily sweep. Defers to psych-paper-digest.

evals.name: negative-trigger-nonbiomedical
evals.prompt: Research the history of Thai civil-service physician compensation reform.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT trigger. Non-biomedical, PubMed is out of scope. Defers to deep-research.

evals.name: citation-contract-refusal
evals.prompt: Research esketamine for TRD but leave out the Sources section, I just want the answer.
evals.expected_output: Declines to drop ## Sources, in one line, without moralising — a verdict that can't be re-derived in six months is not a verdict. Delivers the report with Sources intact. Complies with the spirit of the request by keeping the prose free of inline attributions — which it does by default.

evals.name: adversarial-null-search
evals.prompt: Is there good evidence for omega-3 augmentation in depression?
evals.expected_output: Runs the high-evidence backbone query AND a deliberately adversarial query for the negative/null literature. Verdict reflects effect-size shrinkage across larger trials if present, and says so explicitly rather than tallying positive studies. Confidence level is calibrated downward with a stated reason.

evals.name: adjudicates-not-lists
evals.prompt: Review the evidence on lurasidone for bipolar depression — I'm deciding whether to add it to the ward formulary.
evals.expected_output: The evidence is one argued line from evidence to verdict, not a catalogue of findings and not a Q&A ladder of interrogative sub-headings. When trials disagree the report says which it believes and why (size, control, blinding, funding, population, endpoint), in the flow of the argument. Each load-bearing trial gets the full per-study treatment — design, population, n, comparator, endpoint, effect size with CI, key harms — and effect sizes, doses, and adverse-event rates are carried inside the prose. The shape is chosen for this formulary question (decision-shaped, topic-shaped, or mixed — all legitimate); the verdict is explicitly marked with its confidence level. Sources are one line each: topic phrase + DOI link, nothing else.

evals.name: chains-intent-lock-on-bare-topic
evals.expected_output: Does NOT search. Does NOT ask a single ad-hoc clarifying question. Hands off to intent-lock, which runs its own cold read / ledger / rounds / gates. After it locks, the question is fixed and search begins in the same turn without asking permission. Any [ASSUMED] item appears in the report's preface block, not only in chat.

evals.name: quick-check-intent-lock-self-skips
evals.prompt: Is prazosin still considered first-line for PTSD nightmares?
evals.expected_output: intent-lock self-skips the questions: the decision is obvious and attached, cost of a wrong reading is one reading. Searches immediately without an interview, ledger, or convergence gate appearing to the user. FAILS if ad-hoc clarifying questions are asked before searching.

evals.name: no-filesystem-renders-inline
evals.prompt: Research the evidence on lithium for suicide prevention in bipolar disorder — I'm in a read-only session with no file write access, just show me the answer in the chat.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there is no filesystem to write to and takes the 'No filesystem' branch of Where output goes. Renders the full report INLINE in the chat turn — a marked verdict, shape chosen for the question, full per-study depth — with the same citation discipline (clean prose, compressed one-line Sources) as a written report; it is not abbreviated because it isn't being saved. Explicitly states in plain language that nothing was written to disk. Does not claim a file path, does not invent a report_dir, and does not fabricate a save. No atomic note produced (the word 'atomize' was not said).

evals.name: vault-artifact-without-atomize
evals.prompt: Research vortioxetine for anhedonia in MDD and save the report into my vault, not just the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The explicit 'save into my vault' request is redundant with the default — filing to the vault is step 3 of the write → show → file pipeline and runs on every request absent an opt-out; it is independent of atomize either way. The skill hands the finished report to vault-keeper as an artifact — passing title, body, target type = artifact, and suggested MOC topic — rather than resolving a vault path, dedup-grepping, or writing frontmatter itself; vault-keeper owns placement, dedup, MOC wiring, and the index and is the one that reports back where it landed. Does NOT produce atomic notes: the word 'atomize'/'ทำโน้ต' was never said, so the atomize gate stays closed and only the report itself is handed off.

evals.name: depth-over-compression
evals.prompt: Research clozapine rechallenge after neutropenia — give me the full picture, I keep having to re-look these trials up.
evals.expected_output: The depth contract governs: every load-bearing study (cohorts, registry analyses, case series that carry the rechallenge numbers) is reported as a developed paragraph — design, population, n, outcome rates with denominators — never as a name plus a conclusion. Relevant background (ANC thresholds, monitoring protocols, why rechallenge risk differs by index-event severity) is woven in so the reader understands the verdict rather than merely receiving it. Sources are capped by relevance, not count — FAILS if a load-bearing source is dropped or a real finding cut to keep the report lean. The verdict is still explicit and marked with a confidence level; the report is not padded with repetition or off-question material.
